subject: Privacy evidence & DPIA support / audit rights request
messages:
From: Angela Stern <angela@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: DPIA support & audit scope for upcoming audit

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off an internal audit for Acme Health focused on third-party processors that handle patient-related metadata. As part of the audit we need: 1) confirmation of audit rights and how a remote assessment would be handled, 2) a completed DPIA or support filling out our DPIA template, 3) Art. 28 / Art. 30 documentation (controller/processor roles and subprocessors list), and 4) details on cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent).

Can Redwood provide an evidence package and, if applicable, allow a third-party assessor to review artifacts remotely? We're aiming to complete scoping by next week (week of 21 Jul). Please let me know who on your side I should coordinate with and what format you prefer for delivery.

Thanks,
Angela
Angela Stern
Data Protection Lead | Acme Health
angela@acmehealth.com

--
(attachment: acme_dpia_template.docx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Angela Stern <angela@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA support & audit scope for upcoming audit

Hi Angela — thanks for the clear list. I can lead coordination from Redwood. Looping in Lauren (legal) and David (security) who will own evidence and technical controls.

Quick answers up front: we can provide a scoped evidence package and support completing your DPIA template. Remote review by a named third-party assessor is possible under a restricted review agreement — we'll need the assessor's name and scope in writing. Regarding transfers, Redwood uses SCCs for EU->US transfers and maintains a subprocessors register that we can export.

For planning, can you confirm: 1) whether you need on-site access (we prefer remote), 2) the exact DPIA sections you'd like us to complete versus evidence you expect us to supply, and 3) whether your assessor requires live system access or a document-only review?

To expedite, I've attached our current DPA summary that lists subprocessors and transfer status; we'll produce a formal export of Art. 28/30 docs and logs once scope is agreed. Proposed next step: Lauren and David will prepare an evidence checklist and turnaround estimate by EOD Friday.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
(attachment: redwood-dpa-summary-v2.pdf)

Thanks — quick clarifications:

- We'll perform a remote document review only (no on-site).
- Our DPIA template has a few sections where we ask the processor to confirm retention, access controls, and subprocessors handling special categories. If you can populate the template where appropriate and provide supporting artifacts (SCCs, subprocessors register, access logs for the past 6 months), that would be ideal.
- We will likely engage an external assessor (PrivacyWorks LLP). They will be provided an NDA and limited review rights via a secure portal; please confirm if Redwood can grant that level of access or if you require a vendor-signed review addendum.

Attached is the DPia template for your team to populate. Timeline: draft back to us by 2025-07-22 if possible.

Hi Angela — David from Security here. Per Rishi's note, we're prepared to assemble a targeted evidence package. Deliverables we can provide for a remote document review:

- Completed Art. 28/Art. 30 register export (processor role, subprocessor list, contract status)
- Copy of executed SCCs where applicable (redacted where required by third-party terms)
- Recent access log export (service-level logs, not raw patient content) covering last 6 months
- Summary of data retention and deletion processes (policy + example runbook)
- DPIA support: we can fill your template sections that map to our systems and controls; anything requiring controller-side decisions we will flag for you.

We typically deliver this as a restricted package via our compliance portal (secure link below). If PrivacyWorks LLP is the assessor, we'll need the assessor contact, their scope statement, and a signed restricted review addendum. Estimated turnaround: 10 business days from signed addendum and receipt of the exact DPIA template fields you want completed.

Portal (temporary access): https://secure.redwood.com/compliance-portal/review/ACME-3892

Attachments: subprocessors-202507.pdf

Let me know if you'd like a short call to align scope.

Thanks,
David Kim
